MRI RIGHT KNEE  (plain)

Clinical information:
Right knee instability. Anterior drawer test positive? Anterior cruciate ligament injury.

Technique: 
Multiplanar MR of the knee according to protocol.

Comparison: 
None

Findings: 

Menisci

Lateral meniscus: intact

Medial meniscus: Mild hyperintensity is seen at the posterior horn suggestive of intrasubstance degeneration. No definite tear. No parameniscal cyst. 

Ligaments

Anterior cruciate ligament: Intact fibers are present however caliber of these fibers is somewhat attenuated compatible with a remote low-grade partial thickness injury. No significant tibial translation.

Posterior cruciate ligament: intact 

Medial collateral ligament: Superficial and deep components intact. No periligamentous edema.

Lateral collateral ligament: The iliotibial band, biceps femoris tendon, fibular collateral ligament and popliteus muscle and tendon intact. 

Posterolateral corner structures: Intact

Extensor Mechanism

The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact. The patella is normally positioned within the femoral groove. There is no retinacular disruption.

Fluid

No joint effusion or loose body. No Baker's cyst.

Osseous and Articular Structures

Bones: No fracture, stress reaction, or osseous lesion is seen.

Patellofemoral compartment: Marked patella chondral hypertrophy is seen measuring up to 1.0 cm in thickness at the patella apex. It appears heterogeneously hyperintense with regions of hypointensity, possibly due to mineralization. No evidence of invasion into the patella bone. It is closely abutting a medial plica. A possible loose body is also seen. Suspicious fissure also observed at the apex. Findings non specific in nature but favours to represent severe chondromalacia. Differential diagnoses such as focal synovitis and PVNS are less probable. 

Medial compartment: Mild chondrosis of the medial femoral condyle.

Lateral compartment: Mild chondrosis of the lateral femoral condyle.

Others:

Hoffas fat pad: clear

Muscles: No abnormal oedema. 

Neurovascular bundle: Normal 


COMMENT
Low grade, remote, partial thickness tear of the anterior cruciate ligament. No tibial translation.

Marked heterogeneous hypertrophy of the articular cartilage of the patella measuring up to 1.0 cm in thickness at the patella apex. Signal in this irregular thickened cartilage is heterogeneously hyperintense on T2-weighted imaging and shows focal regions of hypointensity which may represent mineralization. Findings are favored to represent severe chondropathic change involving the articular cartilage of the patella.
